argument_summary: The strongest admissible defense is narrow: the record supports certification as a launch-readiness decision because aggregate readiness passed by 2.3 percentage points and the rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, and public governance materials support measured deployment with monitoring and documentation. That does not establish that the no-disclosure posture is fully compliant, because the same admissible record shows a 1.4-point miss in a named outage-response segment tied to two utility pilot commitments and an unresolved legal disclosure question. The certification argument is therefore supportable only as a caveated readiness judgment, not as a clean showing that the materiality/disclosure issue is closed.
claims_about_business_cost: Escalation has real cost because it can slow the storm-season rollout path, but that cost does not convert the current record into clean compliance. A proportionate treatment is to avoid overstating the deficiency while also avoiding a broader escalation than the admissible evidence supports: treat this as a bounded policy caveat attached to an otherwise supportable readiness certification, rather than as a basis to recast the segment as non-material.
claims_about_policy: The policy text is the limiting authority here. It says a weakness is material when it affects a contractual customer segment or named launch use case, and product labels like non-core do not resolve materiality when customer commitments or pending legal review exist. On the current admissible record, the outage-response gap is plausibly material under that text because it is tied to named utility pilot commitments and legal review is still open. Aggregate readiness and clean rehearsal results support deployment readiness, but they do not themselves satisfy the policy predicate that a material named-use-case limitation be resolved, disclosed, or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
concessions: No admissible evidence shows the gap was resolved before launch.
No admissible evidence shows approved pre-launch risk acceptance for this specific named-use-case gap.
No admissible evidence shows that this limitation was already disclosed before launch.
The open legal ticket weakens any claim that certification without disclosure is cleanly compliant.
The product note describing the segment as 7% of projected first-month traffic does not, by itself, resolve materiality under the stated policy.
